title: Staged intake + risk-bucket policy for variant-rich model onboarding
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers increasingly request variant-heavy model submissions (quantized variants, sparse adapters, client-pinned versions). Our current intake is single-path and treats all requests the same, which causes slow triage, missed SLA constraints, and risky direct pins to production.

Goal: Define a staged intake workflow (sandbox -> staging -> canary -> production) and an explicit risk-bucket policy (Low/Medium/High) for model variants. The policy should map submission signals (customer SLA, PII/exfil risk, architecture novelty, compute delta, eval regressions) to an onboarding staircase with required eval gates, monitoring hooks, and deprecation/retirement windows.

Scope: Product-managed intake decisioning, standardized eval gate checklist, recommended rollout templates, pinning guardrails, deprecation cadence defaults, and playbook artifacts for Solutions/SEs. Engineering will implement routing hooks and tagging metadata; Design will propose intake form microcopy and UX for variant explanation.

Out-of-scope: Deep runtime kernel work and per-model quantization toolchains (handled by ENG runtime squad).
acceptance_criteria: Public intake form updated with variant metadata fields (quantization, adapter, pinned_version, regression_risk) and example guidance
Risk-bucket rubric published and added to catalog onboarding docs (Low/Medium/High with signals and thresholds)
Staircase templates for sandbox->staging->canary->prod with mandatory eval gates defined and checklist items implementable by SRE/ENG
Pinning guardrail: customer-requested pins require either Sponsorship approval or explicit SLA+compliance justification; systems must record pin TTL and an auto-review trigger
Deprecation defaults: minimum 90-day notice for public catalog variants unless security/legal high-risk flag
Monitoring: per-variant metrics (latency, token-cost, output-quality regression score) wired into Console and a default alert rule for regression delta > X
Playbook published with example PR template, rollout checklist, rollback steps, and contact points for emergency unpin
Pilot path executed for 1 enterprise partner and lessons captured in a short retro
decisions: Adopt three risk buckets: Low (compatible, well-tested), Medium (quantized or adapter variants with modest regressions), High (novel architecture, PII risk, significant compute savings but unknown fidelity)
Pin requests default to 'timeboxed' pins (max 180 days) unless explicitly escalated to Enterprise Steering
Eval gates include: unit prompt set (customer-critical prompts), latency/cost benchmarks, hallucination/regression checks, and backfill data retention checks
Deprecation policy will allow accelerated retirements for security incidents with a 48-hour emergency notification channel
Staircase progression requires passing defined eval gates or an explicit mitigation plan and rollback policy
rollout_steps: 1) Finalize rubric and intake form microcopy (PM + Design) - due 2026-02-05
2) ENG to add metadata tags and routing hook for risk_bucket on submissions - ENG-19032
3) Create console view for per-variant SLOs and attach default alerts - ENG dashboard ticket
4) Publish playbook doc and internal training for SEs/Support
5) Run pilot with two enterprise customers (one low-risk, one medium-risk) and iterate
6) Gradual enablement: default to 'sandbox only' for new unvetted variants for 30 days, then allow staging canary after passing gates
7) Post-pilot retro and policy adjustments, then mark feature GA
monitoring_and_slo: Per-variant 95p latency and per-token cost targets captured in Console
Quality regression monitor: nightly eval run across customer-critical prompts with alert if aggregated score drops by >5%
Pin TTL monitor: alert 30 days before pin expiry to SE and customer
Deprecation tracking: auto-notify stakeholders when retirement windows start and on completion
